summary: Calhoun County state forest watch tower on Blue Mountain in Anniston, built 1942-43 and reported in the Anniston Star to 1956; no later record found.

facts.design: Creosoted timber tower with a windowed cab
facts.agency: State Forest Service in the 1940s; the page header lists the Alabama Forestry Commission

staffing.status: Not manned on a regular basis in 1954; Fred Troiano was to man it from October 1956

events.note: Construction reached the 20-foot level in November 1942. The July 1942 plan said 80 feet; the November report said 54 feet above the peak. No completion date in the source.
Lightning strike: all windows smashed and frame damaged; repair estimated at about $75
Shooting damage: 44 of the 48 window panes broken
Funding shortage threatened to remove the area's fire patrolman and close the tower; ranger suggested a $2,000 county contribution, with the State to match local money
Vandals wrecked equipment and window frames on or about 17 October; damage about $100
Anniston Star, 10 October 1956: the tower will be manned by Fred Troiano. A February 1956 plan had listed the tower as one of six posts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The July 1942 plan gives an 80-foot tower (24.4 m in the brief's record) and the November 1942 report gives 54 feet above the peak (16.5 m). The story gives both and the facts leave the height out.

sources.title: Blue Mountain, Forest Lookouts (quoting The Anniston Star, 1942-1956)

notes_for_editor: Single source: newspaper items compiled on the Forest Lookouts site, 1942-1956. No record after October 1956 was found. Searches returned only other Blue Mountains (New York's Blue Mountain Fire Observation Station, Adirondacks), which were not used. Blue Mountain is not on the Alabama lists in the cache (NHLR, 89 lookouts; FFLOS former sites, 34). The brief's height_m 24.4 matches only the 1942 plan, not the finished tower. The page header says Alabama Forestry Commission, but the 1940s items say State Forest Service. Ranger Chandler appears with two different sets of initials (C.B. in 1949, C.D. in 1954); the story uses no initials. Status, access and site condition are unknown: a City of Anniston or Alabama Forestry Commission record would be needed.
